command:change=$(find openspec/changes -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -name archive)
base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
outside=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -v "^$change/" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$outside" ] || { echo "$outside"; echo "the specify stage writes only under $change/ - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: FR8 / D6 policy is applied to only one of the two rules that recommend wall-clock timing. `.claude/rules/bdd-unit.md` (table 'When to Use Unit BDD vs E2E BDD') still says `| Performance (operation time) | yes (performance.now) | no |`. The change updates only `.claude/rules/test-planning.md` and adds ADR 0008. Proposal FR8 says only that 'test-planning.md and ADR 0008 state this policy for future changes'. Impact lists only `.claude/rules/test-planning.md`, and task 7.1 edits only test-planning.md. The next change following bdd-unit.md would bring `performance.now()` assertions back into unit BDD, against FR8/G1. Add bdd-unit.md to the proposal Impact, D6 and task 7.1, with a verification such as `grep -rn "performance.now" .claude/rules` showing only 'never assert' sentences.

Task 6.2 has a manual verification and no automated test, so FR6's warn-and-exit-0 behaviour is unproven. The verification says: 'Then run it on a copy of the JSON with one median edited to 80, passed by path argument: it prints one `::warning` and still exits 0.' This is a one-off manual check. The acceptance criteria require each task to name 'the automated test that proves it under `packages/client/src/`', and test-planning.md says 'The `tasks.md` verification section must list concrete test commands, not "check manually"'. `scripts/check-bench-budgets.mjs` contains real logic: median parsing, the `ROW_BUDGET_MS` comparison, the Markdown summary, `::warning` lines and exit code 0. It needs a Vitest test under `src/` (for example one that runs the script on fixture JSON files with a median under the budget, one over it, and a missing file) and should be covered by a mutation run.

M3 ('Each work-bound scenario fails when the cache it guards is turned off ... a one-off red check per cache during implementation, reverted afterwards') and the 'M3 check' steps in tasks 3 (intro), 3.1, 3.3, 4.2, 4.3 and 5.1 are manual temporary code edits, with no automated, repeatable proof. This conflicts with test-planning.md ('Manual testing ... should be a last resort for things that genuinely cannot be automated') and with the criterion that a task verified by a manual check fails. It can be automated: for example, a Stryker run scoped to ≤5 files (`--mutate 'src/presenter/dateTimeFormatters.ts,src/presenter/dayTrack.ts,src/model/dayPeriodStops.ts,src/presenter/countryName.ts,src/adapters/city-search/zoneCitiesSource.ts'`), with the requirement that the cache-bypass mutants are killed by the work-bound step files. Alternatively, drop the manual-revert wording and make M3 measurable from the mutation report.
